lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
Date of birth: 2 Nov 1996 | Nationality: American
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Improved checkout conversion by 35% after replacing the three-step flow with a one-page flow for all merchants.
- Wrote the requirements and success metrics for dispute self-service, aligning engineering, risk and support; the team shipped it two weeks ahead of plan.
- Interviewed 25 merchants and analysed six months of chargeback data to size annual chargeback losses at 1.1 million dollars, the business case that set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran weekly triage with engineering and support, closing 140 onboarding tickets over the summer and cutting the open-ticket queue by half.
- Measured the onboarding redesign by comparing merchants who opted into the new flow with those who stayed on the old one.
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Mar 2019 - Aug 2023
- Cut late deliveries from 11% to 7% by excluding weather-delayed shipments from the on-time calculation.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Coordinated the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations and prepares the forecast pack for each meeting.
- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots, training 60 drivers and dispatchers and saving 1,800 driver hours a year.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Launched pickup reminders after 60 user interviews showed students missed pickup windows; weekly active users grew from 400 to 1,150 over the following term.
- Set up a volunteer shift system with two dining halls, filling 95% of pickup slots each week and cutting staff cover shifts from 10 to 2 a week.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Held weekly working sessions with clinic managers on outpatient scheduling across the network.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Halved the time it takes a new merchant to receive a first payment, across 2,300 merchants, by redesigning onboarding.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé includes date of birth and nationality, personal details that do not belong on it.
items.because: Readers are not meant to weigh them when assessing qualifications, and they use space unrelated to the work and education.

items.says: The 35% increase is attributed to the flow change and presented as applying to all merchants without evidence of causation or full-base coverage.
items.because: A before-and-after increase does not isolate the flow’s effect or establish that every merchant experienced the uplift.

items.says: The 35% change has no comparison basis.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether it is relative growth or a percentage-point increase, or what period or group it compares.

items.says: Six months of data do not, by themselves, establish annual chargeback losses of 1.1 million dollars.
items.because: The annualization method and loss calculation are not explained.

items.says: The business case and roadmap result are buried after the methods.
items.because: A scanning reader may miss the work’s business impact.

items.says: The opt-in comparison does not establish that the redesign caused the onboarding improvement.
items.because: Merchants who opted in may differ from those who stayed on the old flow.

items.says: The comparison describes how the redesign was measured but gives no result.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the comparison found or whether onboarding improved.

items.says: The change from 9 days to 4 is attributed to the redesign without establishing causation.
items.because: Before-and-after figures do not show what caused the change.

items.says: Excluding weather-delayed shipments changes the calculation, not necessarily the number of late deliveries.
items.because: The 11% and 7% rates are comparable only if both use the same inclusion criteria.

items.says: The 30% reduction has no baseline or measurement period.
items.because: Readers cannot gauge the change without the starting and ending rates or understand how it was measured.

items.says: The bullet switches from past to present tense in an ended role.
items.because: The shift makes the timeline of the forecast-pack responsibility unclear.

items.says: The 1,800 annual driver hours are presented as realized savings without saying whether they were measured or estimated.
items.because: An annualized estimate is not the same as verified hours saved.

items.says: The strongest result appears after the rollout and training details.
items.because: Readers scanning the bullet may miss the 1,800-hour result.

items.says: “That would have been thrown away” repeats the surplus-food context.
items.because: It lengthens the result without adding a distinct detail.

items.says: The timing may imply that pickup reminders caused the growth in weekly active users.
items.because: Growth after launch does not establish causation, and the interviews do not show how prevalent missed pickups were among students generally.

items.says: Passive wording hides who mapped intake and shortened the form.
items.because: Readers cannot tell what the candidate contributed to the practicum.

items.says: The adoption result appears after the methods instead of leading the bullet.
items.because: Scanning readers see the process changes before learning that front-desk staff adopted them.

items.says: The practicum bullet assigns a merchant-onboarding result to a hospital project.
items.because: The other practicum bullets concern clinics, while merchant onboarding is a payments-platform activity.

items.says: The same onboarding achievement is attributed to two roles with conflicting reductions.
items.because: Harbor Payments reports 9 days to 4 across 2,300 merchants, while the practicum calls the same result a halving.

items.says: “Halved” is numerically wrong for a change from 9 days to 4 days.
items.because: Half of 9 days is 4.5 days; the reported change is about a 56% reduction.
